title: Promotion & digital marketing
examples: What is the difference between a metric and a goal in marketing?
How do I know if an influencer partnership is actually worth the money?
Can you give an example of a successful social media campaign for a small local shop?

explain.say: Today we are learning about promoting things using digital marketing tools. Promotion means telling people about your product or service. Digital marketing uses online methods to reach customers.
Social media platforms are popular ways to promote businesses today. These sites allow companies to share updates and connect directly with people. Think about platforms like Instagram or TikTok.
Influencers are people who have a large following online. Brands pay them to promote their products to their dedicated audience. This can seem very trustworthy to followers.
Metrics are simply ways to measure how well your promotion is working. They give you numbers so you know what to improve next time. Examples include likes or website visits.

items: Reach | How many people saw it

explain.say: A real-life example is a local bakery promoting a new cake flavor. They post beautiful photos on Instagram and ask a local food blogger to try it. They then count the comments to see interest.
A common mistake is only looking at the number of likes. You must also check the comments to see if people are actually buying the cake. Look at the quality, not just the quantity.

draw.text: Look at comments, not just likes

faq.q: What is the difference between reach and impressions?
faq.a: Reach is the number of unique people who saw your content. Impressions is the total number of times your content was seen, even by the same person.
asks: What is the difference between unique viewers and total views?
Can I get more reach on my posts?

faq.q: Do I need to pay influencers or can I just send them free products?
faq.a: While free products can help, paid partnerships often guarantee the required level of promotion. The agreement should always be clear.
asks: Is it better to pay or trade products?
How much should I pay an influencer?

faq.q: Which social media platform is best for selling clothes?
faq.a: Instagram is often very good for visual products like clothes because of its photo and video focus. However, TikTok is also growing in this area.
asks: Should I use TikTok or Instagram for fashion?
What platform is best for visual marketing?

faq.q: What is 'engagement rate' and why is it important?
faq.a: Engagement rate measures how much your audience interacts with your content compared to how many people see it. A high rate shows your content is interesting.
asks: How do I calculate engagement rate?

faq.q: If my promotion fails, what should I do next?
faq.a: You must look closely at your metrics. Did the wrong audience see it, or was the message unclear? Use the data to adjust your next attempt.
asks: How do I fix a bad marketing campaign?
What data tells me what went wrong?

facts: Social media allows businesses to build a community around their brand.
Influencers build credibility through their established trust with their followers.
Metrics like 'conversion rate' track how many people take a desired action.
A strong promotional strategy combines multiple digital channels for maximum effect.

quiz.say: A company wants to know how many unique people saw their latest ad. Which metric should they check?
quiz.show: Unique people who saw the ad
quiz.why: Reach specifically counts the number of different people who viewed the content at least once.

wrong.0: Engagement only measures actions like likes or comments, not just viewing the ad.
wrong.1: Conversion measures if the person completed a final action, like buying something.
wrong.3: Impressions count every single time the ad was displayed, which might count the same person multiple times.

quiz.say: A small bookstore uses a local book reviewer on YouTube to promote a new book. This reviewer is acting as a:
quiz.why: A micro-influencer is someone with a smaller, highly engaged following who seems very trustworthy to their niche audience.

wrong.0: A metric is just a measurement, like the view count, not the person doing the promotion.
wrong.2: An advertiser is the business paying for the promotion, not the person doing the promotion.
wrong.3: A platform is the website itself, like YouTube, not the person creating the content.

quiz.say: If a marketing campaign has 1000 total views and 50 comments, what is the basic engagement rate?
quiz.why: Engagement rate is often calculated by dividing total interactions by total reach, giving a percentage.

wrong.0: This incorrectly divides the total views by the number of comments.
wrong.1: This incorrectly multiplies the two numbers together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly assumes the number of comments is the total interaction figure.
